start.text: The great hall of the Ember Palace is hot as a summer noon. Courtiers in masks of gilt and feathers dance in their shirtsleeves under a thousand candles, and nobody mentions the frost on the outside of the windows. At the far end, beside the empty throne, a lean grey man in plain black sits in a plain chair with a glass of wine, watching the dancers as a shepherd watches sheep. When he sees you, he smiles and lifts the glass an inch. Lord Regent Varric Caul has been expecting you.

choices.text: Step aside and let Corin face him.
Look up at the gallery and give the Order of Ash its signal.
[Persuasion] Climb onto the musicians' dais, hold up the Greyford satchel and read the order aloud.
[Insight] Sit down beside him and ask, quietly, where the Queen really went.
Hear what he has to say.

corin_faces.speaker: corin
corin_faces.text: Corin walks the length of the hall in his scraped plate and the dancers part in front of him. 'Lord Marshal,' he says. Caul looks up, mild. 'Edric's boy. You blew a fine horn.' Corin takes the note out of the satchel and reads it, loud enough for the gallery: 'To the horn-post only. Halvard is not to see it. V. C.' Then he holds it out. 'Your hand, my lord. Your seal. Ten knights and forty-one people of Tarrow.' At the edge of the floor, the captain of the Knives says, flatly, 'That's the Marshal's seal. I served under it.'

order.text: You look up. In the gallery above the dancers, a row of masked guests take off their masks, and under them are the faces of the Order of Ash, and over their shoulders the reversed shields of Emberhold turned face out. Lord-Commander Edric Ashdown comes down the gallery stair in his black, and the music stops of its own accord. You put the satchel in his hands. He reads the order and the note aloud in a voice made for parade grounds, gives the satchel back to you, and then he says, 'Varric Caul, the Order of Ash names you forsworn.'

exposed.text: The hall goes silent, a silence so complete you can hear the candles. Then a masked lady near you takes off her mask and drops it on the floor, and a lord beside her does the same, and the sound of masks falling goes round the room like the first drops of rain. Caul sets down his glass. 'Well,' he says pleasantly, to nobody. 'Then we shall have to do this privately.' He walks behind the throne and down a narrow stair into the hill, and when two of his Knives move to follow him, their captain puts out an arm and stops them.

laughed.text: You read it well, but Caul laughs before you are halfway through: a warm, delighted, genuine laugh, and the court laughs with him because the court always laughs with him. 'A forged order, forged by me, proved by a forgery? My dear, the Marches have been at you.' He stands and bows to the room. 'Forgive me. I must see to the furnaces.' He goes behind the throne and down a narrow stair, and four Knives close in behind him to guard it.

slip.speaker: highspire_caul
slip.text: For half a breath the courtier slips and something older looks out of his face. 'North,' he says, very quietly. 'She broke the stone with a hammer from the Collegium kitchens and walked north into the briars, and I could not stop her, and I could not follow her.' Then he is himself again, smiling. 'She died in her sleep. It is in the proclamation.'

offer.speaker: highspire_caul
offer.text: 'You have been very busy,' Caul says. 'Brightwater, the Wood, Saltmere, the Marches. You have pieces of my stone, I think. With them, it would keep this city warm for ten more years.' He turns his glass. 'Bring them to me and I will make you Lord Marshal. Or keep them, and freeze with everyone else. Either way, it has been a pleasure.' He rises, bows, and goes behind the throne, down a narrow stair into the hill, and four Knives close in to guard it.

choices.text: [Persuasion] Before he reaches the stair, hold up the Greyford satchel and read the order aloud to the court.
Let him go. You know where he went.

start.speaker: highspire_caul
start.text: Varric Caul sits on a stool beside the glass cage with his coat off and frost in his hair, one hand resting on the glass as a man rests his hand on a sleeping dog. He does not get up. 'She broke it herself, you know. Isolde. She knew I wanted it, and she knew it was dying, so she broke three pieces off and sent them away where I would never think to look, and she walked north into the Thornwake with nothing. She is still up there. The Thorn Queen, the refugees call her. She is holding the cold back with her own body.' He looks at the stone. 'I kept the heart. A city should not die for one woman's gesture.'

choices.text: [Persuasion] 'It's over, Varric. Your court has seen the order. Your own Knives let me through.'
[Persuasion] 'She is holding it back alone. Give her what she needs to stop.'
[Arcana] 'Look at your hands, Varric. The stone isn't only warming the palace. It's drinking you.'

mirela_speaks.speaker: mirela
mirela_speaks.text: Mirela steps past you to the cage, and Caul's face does something you have not seen it do: it softens. 'My clever girl.' 'Don't,' Mirela says. 'I did the figures, Varric. I did them every morning on that orrery for you, and I moved the frost forward by hand. Eleven months for Highspire, and the stone gone grey, and you with it. You are not saving the city. You are keeping one room warm while the house burns.' Her voice does not shake. 'Give it to me. You taught me to know when the sums are finished.'

fight.speaker: highspire_caul
fight.text: Caul sighs, and stands, and takes a long knife from inside his coat. 'I was afraid you would say something like that.' He opens the cage and closes his bare hand round the heart-stone, and the frost on the walls sighs inward toward him. He does not call for his Knives. Whatever happens down here, he means it to happen between the two of you.

yield.text: For a long time Varric Caul says nothing at all. Then he takes a key on a chain from round his neck, opens the cage, and lifts the heart-stone out on its velvet in both hands, the way you would lift something newborn. Above you, very faintly, the palace begins to get colder. 'Take it, then,' he says. 'I am so tired of holding it.' He puts it in your hands and goes down on his knees in the frost.

start.text: Varric Caul kneels in the frost with his hands open on his knees. Without the stone he looks exactly his age, and colder than anyone you have ever seen. 'Well?' he says. 'Kings of Vael have hanged men for less. You have the crown's heart in your hands. That makes it your decision, I suppose.'

choices.text: End him, here, where no one will see.
End him. The court has already judged him.
'The court can judge you.' Call for Captain Dunmore.
'Go north, Varric. Go and see what she is holding back.' Take his signet and let him walk out.

killed_secret.text: It is quick, and he does not resist. When it is done you take the red-gold signet from his hand, because it was never his. Upstairs, the Masque goes on for another hour before anybody wonders where the Regent went. By morning there are three different stories about it in Lowtown, and in two of them it was you.

killed_public.text: It is quick, and he does not resist; he even turns his head a little, to make it easier. You take the red-gold signet from his hand, because it was never his. When you carry the heart-stone up the private stair, Captain Dunmore is waiting at the top with his knife-badge in his pocket. He looks past you, down into the dark, and nods once, and says nothing at all.

court.text: Captain Dunmore comes down the stair with two of his Knives and takes the Regent by the arm, almost gently. Caul gives you his signet without being asked. 'The Quiet Cells, Captain,' he says. 'I signed the order for every lock down there. I may as well admire them.' At the top of the stair, Dunmore looks back at you. 'There'll be a trial,' he says. 'First honest one in this city since the Queen died.'

mirela_binds.speaker: mirela
mirela_binds.text: Mirela kneels in front of him, takes his signet off his finger and gives it to you without looking. Then she lays her hands on his shoulders and speaks a word, and frost runs from her fingers over his coat, not cold but clear, like glass. 'The Quiet Cells,' she says. 'You built them on my figures. You can sit in one and think about what you did with them.' Caul looks up at her with something like pride, which is the worst thing you have seen all night.

exiled.text: Caul looks at you a long moment, and then he laughs, softly, without any malice at all. 'North. Yes. That is crueller than a knife, and kinder.' He gives you the signet, gets to his feet like an old man, and goes down the cistern stair into the dark of the aqueduct without his coat. You do not think you will see him again. You are not sure.
